questions.question: What is the vtable mechanism in C++ and how does it enable runtime polymorphism?
options: A variable table created per object at runtime to store member values
A compile-time per-class table of virtual function pointers; each object holds a vptr to its class vtable — at runtime the dispatcher follows vptr to call the correct override
A runtime table rebuilt on every virtual function call
A debug table used only when running under a debugger
questions.answer: A compile-time per-class table of virtual function pointers; each object holds a vptr to its class vtable — at runtime the dispatcher follows vptr to call the correct override

questions.question: What is the diamond problem in C++ and how does virtual inheritance resolve it?
options: Two base classes have the same method name — resolved by overloading
When D inherits B and C which both inherit Base, D gets two Base subobjects causing ambiguity — virtual inheritance makes B and C share a single Base subobject in D
A derived class overrides a virtual function incorrectly
Multiple constructors conflict — resolved by the explicit keyword
questions.answer: When D inherits B and C which both inherit Base, D gets two Base subobjects causing ambiguity — virtual inheritance makes B and C share a single Base subobject in D

questions.question: What is move semantics in C++11 and what problem does it solve?
options: Moves objects between different regions of the stack
Transfers resource ownership from a temporary rvalue without deep copying — eliminates expensive unnecessary copies for short-lived objects
Automatically frees memory when an object moves out of scope
Allows objects to change their declared type at runtime
questions.answer: Transfers resource ownership from a temporary rvalue without deep copying — eliminates expensive unnecessary copies for short-lived objects

questions.question: What is the Rule of Three/Five in C++ and when is it mandatory?
options: If any of destructor, copy constructor, or copy assignment is user-defined, all three (or five including move operations in C++11) should be defined — mandatory when a class manages raw resources
All classes must define exactly three or five constructors
A class can inherit from at most three base classes
Applies only to classes that use template parameters
questions.answer: If any of destructor, copy constructor, or copy assignment is user-defined, all three (or five including move operations in C++11) should be defined — mandatory when a class manages raw resources

questions.question: What is a reference in C++ and how does it differ from a pointer?
options: A reference and pointer are identical in every way

A reference is an alias for an existing variable — cannot be null, cannot be reseated after initialization, requires no dereferencing syntax; a pointer can be null, reassigned, and requires * to dereference
A reference can be reseated to point to a different variable; a pointer cannot
References require the * operator to access the stored value
questions.answer: A reference is an alias for an existing variable — cannot be null, cannot be reseated after initialization, requires no dereferencing syntax; a pointer can be null, reassigned, and requires * to dereference

questions.question: What is a pure virtual function and what does declaring one do to the class?
options: A virtual function with an empty body {}
A virtual function declared with =0 — the class becomes abstract and cannot be instantiated directly; all concrete derived classes must provide an override
A virtual function that cannot be overridden in any derived class
A static function that behaves polymorphically
questions.answer: A virtual function declared with =0 — the class becomes abstract and cannot be instantiated directly; all concrete derived classes must provide an override
questions.topic: Pure virtual functions and abstract classes

questions.question: What is the 'this' pointer in C++ and in which context is it available?
options: A pointer to the class definition stored globally
An implicit pointer available inside non-static member functions that points to the object on which the member function was invoked
A pointer to the parent class subobject
A global pointer that always points to the most recently created object
questions.answer: An implicit pointer available inside non-static member functions that points to the object on which the member function was invoked

questions.question: What is function prototyping in C++ and why is it necessary?
options: Defining a function with its full body before main()
A forward declaration specifying the function's name, return type, and parameter types — allows the compiler to validate calls made before the full definition appears in the source file
A technique to make any function inline automatically
A way to overload functions using different return types
questions.answer: A forward declaration specifying the function's name, return type, and parameter types — allows the compiler to validate calls made before the full definition appears in the source file

questions.question: What is the difference between a while loop and a do-while loop in C++?
options: There is no difference — both evaluate the condition before each iteration
while evaluates the condition before the body — may execute zero times if initially false; do-while evaluates the condition after the body — always executes at least once
do-while evaluates the condition before the body; while evaluates after
while can only iterate a fixed number of times; do-while can iterate indefinitely
questions.answer: while evaluates the condition before the body — may execute zero times if initially false; do-while evaluates the condition after the body — always executes at least once

questions.question: What is operator overloading in C++ and which operator cannot be overloaded?

All operators can be overloaded without restriction in C++
Operator overloading is only permitted for arithmetic operators
The assignment operator = cannot be overloaded

questions.question: What is a copy constructor in C++ and when is it automatically invoked?

A constructor that initializes a new object as a copy of an existing object — automatically invoked during object initialization from another object, pass-by-value, and return-by-value
A constructor that only copies static data members
A constructor invoked exclusively when the = assignment operator is used on two existing objects
questions.answer: A constructor that initializes a new object as a copy of an existing object — automatically invoked during object initialization from another object, pass-by-value, and return-by-value

options: Only single and multiple inheritance
Single, multiple, multilevel, hierarchical, and hybrid inheritance
Single, multilevel, and hierarchical inheritance only
Single, multiple, hierarchical, and template inheritance

questions.question: What is the purpose of the delete[] operator in C++ compared to delete?
options: delete and delete[] are completely interchangeable
delete frees a single object allocated with new; delete[] frees an array allocated with new[] and calls destructors for each element — mixing them is undefined behavior
delete[] frees a single object; delete frees an array
delete[] is only needed for arrays of primitive types
questions.answer: delete frees a single object allocated with new; delete[] frees an array allocated with new[] and calls destructors for each element — mixing them is undefined behavior

questions.question: What is the difference between stack memory and heap memory in C++?
options: Both store the same types of data with no performance difference

Stack is automatically managed (LIFO), fast, and stores local variables and function frames; heap is manually managed (new/delete), slower, and stores dynamically allocated objects that outlive function scope
Heap memory is faster than stack memory
Stack memory persists for the lifetime of the program; heap memory is destroyed after each function returns
questions.answer: Stack is automatically managed (LIFO), fast, and stores local variables and function frames; heap is manually managed (new/delete), slower, and stores dynamically allocated objects that outlive function scope

questions.question: What is const correctness in C++ and why is it important?
options: const is useful only for compile-time integer constants and has no effect on class design

Marking member functions and parameters const prevents accidental modification, enables compiler optimizations, documents intent, and allows const objects to invoke only const-qualified member functions
const member functions cannot have any return value
const correctness applies only to global variables and static members
questions.answer: Marking member functions and parameters const prevents accidental modification, enables compiler optimizations, documents intent, and allows const objects to invoke only const-qualified member functions

questions.question: What is the STL and what are its three main components?

STL (Standard Template Library) provides containers (vector, map, set, etc.), algorithms (sort, find, etc.), and iterators — enabling generic, reusable, and efficient data structure and algorithm implementations
STL provides only sorting and searching algorithms for primitive types
STL is a third-party library that must be installed separately from the C++ compiler
questions.answer: STL (Standard Template Library) provides containers (vector, map, set, etc.), algorithms (sort, find, etc.), and iterators — enabling generic, reusable, and efficient data structure and algorithm implementations

questions.question: What is the difference between struct and class in C++?
options: struct cannot have member functions or inheritance
struct members are public by default; class members are private by default — otherwise both support member functions, constructors, inheritance, and all OOP features
class cannot be used with inheritance
struct is provided only for C backward compatibility
questions.answer: struct members are public by default; class members are private by default — otherwise both support member functions, constructors, inheritance, and all OOP features

questions.question: What is exception handling in C++ and what are the three keywords used?
options: A compile-time feature using #pragma, #error, and #warning
A runtime mechanism using try (marks the guarded block), throw (signals an error by creating an exception object), and catch (handles the exception)
A technique that prevents all runtime errors from occurring
A debugging feature using static_assert, noexcept, and abort()
questions.answer: A runtime mechanism using try (marks the guarded block), throw (signals an error by creating an exception object), and catch (handles the exception)

questions.question: What is enumeration in C++ and how does enum class differ from a plain enum?
options: They are identical — enum class is only an alias
Plain enum values leak into the enclosing scope and implicitly convert to int; enum class provides scoped values (accessed via ::) that do not implicitly convert to int, preventing name clashes
enum class is only available starting in C++17
Plain enum prevents name clashes; enum class introduces them
questions.answer: Plain enum values leak into the enclosing scope and implicitly convert to int; enum class provides scoped values (accessed via ::) that do not implicitly convert to int, preventing name clashes

questions.question: What is noexcept in C++11 and what happens if a noexcept function throws?
options: noexcept means the function must always throw an exception
noexcept specifies that a function will not throw — if it does, std::terminate() is called immediately; it enables compiler optimizations and communicates intent to callers
noexcept is equivalent to wrapping the function body in try-catch
noexcept only applies to destructors and is ignored on other functions
questions.answer: noexcept specifies that a function will not throw — if it does, std::terminate() is called immediately; it enables compiler optimizations and communicates intent to callers
